paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. There are two groups in this chapter, and only one of them gets to stand with the Lamb. The 144,000 have His name and His Father's name on their foreheads, and they "follow the Lamb wherever He goes" (Revelation 14:1, 4). Meanwhile, the beast's mark leads to the wine of God's anger (Revelation 14:9-10). So the question for me and for you is simple: whose name are we carrying?

Now, this passage is heavy, and I won't pretend otherwise. But look at how it handles the heavy. Before the judgment comes, an angel flies over every nation and tribe and tongue and people with the eternal gospel, saying to worship the One who made everything (Revelation 14:6-7). I think that means God is not hiding the warning. He's shouting it from the sky, and that tells me He wants people to hear it.

And for those who belong to Him, there's a word just for them: "Here is a call for the perseverance of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus" (Revelation 14:12). Then comes a promise: "they will rest from their labors, for their deeds will follow them" (Revelation 14:13). Friend, I spent years in the back of a drawer thinking nobody was keeping track of me, and I was WRONG. Keep going, keep following the Lamb, and keep your ovens ready, because the One on the cloud is the One who sees every bit of it.
